definitions.explanation: To clean a surface by brushing away dirt, dust, or debris with a broom.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{玄関|げんかん}を{掃|は}く。
examples.english: I sweep the entrance every morning.

examples.japanese: {落|お}ち{葉|ば}を{掃|は}いて{集|あつ}めた。
examples.english: I swept up and gathered the fallen leaves.

examples.japanese: {掃|は}いても{掃|は}いても{砂|すな}が{入|はい}ってくる。
examples.english: No matter how much I sweep, sand keeps coming in.

notes:
{掃|は}く is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) specifically for sweeping with a broom.

ASPECT (ている):
{掃|は}いている indicates sweeping is in progress.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [place]を{掃|は}く — to sweep [place]
- [debris]を{掃|は}く — to sweep up [debris]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {床|ゆか}を{掃|は}く (sweep the floor)
- {庭|にわ}を{掃|は}く (sweep the garden)
- {掃|は}き{掃除|そうじ} (sweeping)
- {掃|は}き{出|だ}し{窓|まど} (sliding glass door - opens to swept area)

DO NOT CONFUSE:
- {掃|は}く (to sweep) — different from:
- {履|は}く (to put on pants/shoes)
- {吐|は}く (to vomit, exhale)

All three are read はく but have different kanji and meanings.

RELATED WORD:
{箒|ほうき} (broom)
